messages:
rachel: FYI seeing repeated 95/99.9p tail for small-gen workloads on uswest2-shelf07. numbers spike when tenant 'vecify' runs multi-concurrent small inferences.

tom: is this network or GPU? rack-level or node-local?

rachel: quick triage: GPU util fine, but PCIe rx drop counters climbing + host CPU softirq up. looks like PCIe switch fabric saturation on shelf07-slot3.

ajay: ugh noisy tenant again? vecify runs lots of tiny memcpy+kernel launches, lots of PCIe RTS. scheduling might be packing them onto same PCIe switch.

maya: can we repro with fio / microbench? wonder if NUMA pinning + colocated replicas cause backpressure.

rachel: local probe logs:

rachel: ```
$ nvidia-smi dmon -s u 
# saw 2-3k memcpy ops/sec per GPU during bursts
$ ethtool -S pcie0 | grep rx_drop
rx_drop: 4162
$ dmesg | tail -n 5
pcieport 0000:5e:00.0: AER: Corrected error received: ROLLOVER
```

tom: scheduler view? are we packing multiple small tenants that generate a lot of PCIe traffic on same switch?

scheduler-bot: Current placement heuristic: prefer-binpack on shelf07 (score=0.78). Detected co-locates: vecify (3 pods) + dataset-persist (2 pods) on switch sw-5e.

ajay: suggest quick policy change: anti-coalesce for small-gen workloads (label: run.small-gen) to spread across PCIe domains. That should reduce per-switch churn.

maya: spread helps latency but may increase egress costs + inter-rack traffic if we cross ToR. tradeoff noted.

rachel: ops, can we flip anti-coalesce for 30m and watch tail? Also, is there a cheaper routing tweak to avoid spilling to neighboring racks?

ops-runner: Applied scheduling override: anti-coalesce rule for job label run.small-gen = true, ttl=40m. Also set placement soft-penalty for sw-5e weight=0.15. Monitoring now.

tom: nice. what's observed after 10m?

rachel: after rule applied, 95th/99.9th down ~35ms and 99.99th down ~200ms on affected slots. PCIe rx_drop counters still rising slowly but much less churn.

ajay: long-term: need to teach placer to be PCIe-aware (topology-aware scoring) and honor 'micro-burst' profiles. Also maybe an admission control for tiny high-IO tenants.

maya: +1. but customers will ask about cost: if we force spread, they may need dedicated slices to get predictable latency. want to prepare a short cost comparison (shared w/ anti-coalesce vs fractional dedicated).

rachel: initial back-of-envelope: anti-coalesce increases cross-rack traffic modestly for these workloads (~5% packet increase) but reduces tail-induced retries and token-cost due to timeouts. Dedicated slice quarter cost is ~2.5x per-hour but buys deterministic slots.

tom: can we auto-detect tenants that benefit from dedicated (latency-sensitive microburst) and nudge them via UX? scheduler-bot can emit placement-risk metric.

scheduler-bot: New metric emitted: placement.risk.microburst for tenant vecify=0.87 (high). Recommend dedicated:slice offer.

ops-runner: created INFRA-2610 (plc: PCIe topology-aware scoring), INFRA-2611 (proto: microburst admission control), COST-781 (pricing brief for fractional dedicated vs spread policy).

rachel: leaving anti-coalesce in place for 40m. will follow up with a quick runbook for oncall: how to throttle/soft-pin noisy tenants before they cause slab churn.

ajay: one more mitigation to consider: limit concurrent shards per PCIe switch via scheduler soft cap (eg max 2 small-gen pods per PCIe domain). Less disruptive than full dedicated.

maya: agree. add as follow-up. I'll draft the customer note about why they might see spread and what dedicated gets them.

rachel: thanks all. keep an eye on shelf07 -- ping here if 99.9th jumps. :eyes:
